summary.title: SLAI T-Rex: Full-Parameter Post-training of the DeepSeek-V4 Family on Ascend SuperPOD

setting_and_object.category: System / framework technical report (training-infrastructure + domain post-training recipe)

details: Full-parameter post-training of trillion-parameter MoE models with hybrid sparse attention is almost exclusively done on CUDA/TPU stacks; doing it on SIMD-oriented Ascend NPU SuperPODs is unexplored, and Operations Research (OR) is an under-served target domain for such post-training.

SLAI T-Rex: an integrated full-stack post-training framework for the DeepSeek-V4 family on Ascend CloudMatrix384 SuperPOD, combining (i) hierarchical system optimization — parallelism/communication orchestration (expert-tensor parallelism folding, asynchronous MoE all-to-all with shared-expert overlap, double-buffered swap optimizer), plus kernel-level work, and (ii) solver-grounded CPT+SFT specialization for OR.

AuraKernel: an AscendC kernel-optimization agent whose defining mechanism is an operations-research solver that picks tiling by minimizing the maximum per-pipeline-stage cycle cost (MTE1/MTE2/MAC/FixPipe/scalar) under on-chip capacity constraints, used to initialize a hardware-verified, branch-and-rollback search loop with skill distillation.

OR data engine: bidirectional, Gurobi-verified synthesis — parameterized optimization instances are solved, rendered into business-style natural-language problems, re-modeled forward into executable programs, and accepted only when the reconstructed program reproduces the reference objective.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T parameters, large MoE + hybrid sparse attention) trained full-parameter on Ascend CloudMatrix384 SuperPOD with Ascend 910C NPUs (64 GB HBM each); global batch size 1024.

Attention at TP=2 with MoE ETP=1 via Megatron-style MoE Parallel Folding; PP=8 using virtual pipeline parallelism (VPP) instead of DualPipeV, justified by peak reserved memory of 51.7–54.6 GB per NPU under VPP.
Distributed AdamW with a chunked, double-buffered host-offload (swap) optimizer overlapping swap-in/swap-out streams with fused update kernels.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash used as the primary experimentation platform for the OR workflow; CPT executed via MindSpeed and TorchTitan-NPU routes with context and expert parallelism.
One representative training step: 206,503 compute-kernel launches, 39.84 s device compute after excluding communication and AI-CPU; communication is 40.76 s (52.2% of device kernel time).
Per-operator AIC/AIV counters (MAC, vector compute, MTE2 load, MTE3/FixPipe store, cube/scalar utilization) used to classify kernels as compute-, memory-, or control-bound.

AuraKernel harness: isolated parallel sandboxes on real NPUs, JSON-over-HTTP tools, read-only accuracy tests as a correctness gate, acceptance requiring 2% measured speedup plus content-hash deduplication, and rules forbidding moving computation outside the measured kernel or swapping operator paradigm.

K-Search tree search over optimization directions with UCB-style leaf selection (expected gain, exploration, difficulty), sibling-priority back-propagation, checkpoint rollback, and three-layer context compression; verified gains distilled into (pre-metric, metric-delta, transformation) skills retrieved by cosine similarity.

Fusion/rewrite targets re-expressed as UB-resident AscendC kernels: mHC suite (weight-free RMSNorm fwd/bwd, pre/post weighted-expansion BMM), limited-SwiGLU backward including the MoE routing-weight gradient reduction, unified rotary embedding (q/kv/o with cached cos/sin), and a BF16-at-global-memory mixed-precision dataflow for the mHC pre-projection.

CPT corpus: ~100K OR documents combining solver-verified synthetic modeling documents (generators for assignment, scheduling, facility location, network flow, production/lot sizing, routing, covering, transportation, portfolio, revenue management) with collected resources (OptMATH, OR-Instruct, OptiBench/ReSocratic, NLP4LP, ORQA-derived, MAMO, Gurobi examples, papers/textbooks); domain-dominant mixture supplemented with AutoMathText-V2 math, Nemotron code, and Ultra-FineWeb-L3 English.

SFT: cyclic self-distillation with L1 canonical / L2 semantic / L3 synthetic intermediate representations, three data-presentation modes (data in problem, data in table, data-problem separate), leakage-control and semantic-similarity filters, and an accepted-IR flywheel; 3K / 10K / 50K scales compared, with 10K selected for contract-aware cleaning and CoT enhancement.

Checkpoint selection by OR held-out likelihood, general-capability retention, and matched CPT-to-SFT transfer gain (Route A: base->SFT vs Route B: base->CPT->SFT with identical SFT data and optimization).
Four OR benchmarks: NL4OPT, OptiBench, Bench4Opt-Feasible (objective-value match) and Bench4Opt-ORGEval (structural equivalence via WL reward).
Diagnostic settings on the base checkpoint: Pass@1, Pass@16, 5-shot, with 1,456 failed cases manually grouped into seven error families.
Comparison points: original DeepSeek-V4-Flash, GPT-5.4-Mini, and scale-up to DeepSeek-V4-Pro.

key_findings.finding: Full-stack Ascend-native optimization nearly triples training efficiency for a 1.6T-parameter MoE model.
key_findings.evidence: MFU of DeepSeek-V4-Pro rises from 11.67% under open-source baseline recipes to 34.22% (2.93x) after optimized parallelism, NPU-CPU co-optimization, and kernel optimization, while maintaining training stability.

key_findings.finding: CPT and SFT play complementary roles: SFT fixes protocol/executability behavior while CPT initialization supplies the structural OR modeling prior, with the largest additional gain on structural equivalence.
key_findings.evidence: Under matched SFT data and optimization on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, direct SFT lifts B4O-Feasible 60.47->65.93 and B4O-ORGEval 34.26->48.73; CPT-then-SFT lifts them further to 71.22 and 59.39. The final model averages 71.81% over four OR benchmarks, +3.98 points over GPT-5.4-Mini and +11.27 over the base model; applying the workflow to DeepSeek-V4-Pro raises its average from 70.16% to 77.33%.

key_findings.finding: On Ascend SuperPOD the MoE all-to-all is not the bottleneck; pipeline point-to-point and TP/DP reductions dominate communication, and sparse-attention kernels are memory/control-bound rather than compute-bound, which directly changes the optimal schedule choice.
key_findings.evidence: Communication is 52.2% of device kernel time, split as TP/DP AllReduce-AllGather-ReduceScatter 48.4%, pipeline Send/Receive 36.7%, expert AllToAllV only 14.5%. SparseAttnSharedkvGrad is the top single kernel at 16.86% of compute time with ~9.5% vector-compute pipeline ratio, versus GroupedMatmul at 86.8% MAC and ~95% cube utilization. Because DualPipeV targets the 14.5% all-to-all while roughly doubling resident chunks against a measured 51.7-54.6 GB peak, VPP is chosen instead.

key_findings.finding: An OR-solver-guided, hardware-verified agent yields substantial speedups on complex AscendC kernels, and the gains come from cutting global-memory traffic rather than raising compute utilization.
key_findings.evidence: The tiling solver alone reduces MatMul execution time by 6.55% across common LLM shapes; AuraKernel accelerates the shared-KV sparse-attention backward by up to 1.24x in its end-to-end training context and, in one campaign, optimizes 14 reduction-heavy framework operators to full correctness with 2.06x average and 11.90x best speedup.
